options.description: Keeps today's behaviour. Only the sentences a record quotes from you go into git with the record; your full messages stay private. The older choice is narrowed to say that.
options.label: Commit only the quoted words (Recommended)

options.description: No words of yours are committed. The judge reads them only from this machine's session log, and a fresh clone can't judge until it has them. Needs a rewrite of the judge's input and its tests before landing.
options.label: Nothing of my words in git

payload.question: Two older choices disagree about where the judge reads your words from. One says your messages stay only in this machine's private session log and are never committed to git. The judge's code, which has worked this way since early October, commits the words a record quotes from you next to that record, so a fresh clone can still judge. Which should hold?
